messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about MEDIA, COMMUNICATION AND LANGUAGE and SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS in Illinois during the 1940s, matching this research need: survey data on opinion leaders’ influence on consumer behavior, fashion, political attitudes, moviegoing, media use, social networks, and named influential contacts, including follow-up interviews with those identified opinion leaders
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: Decatur Illinois 1945 opinion leadership survey named influential contacts follow up interviews dataset
ICPSR Decatur study personal influence 1945 women opinion leaders dataset
action.query: Decatur Illinois 1945 opinion leadership survey named influential contacts follow up interviews dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Decatur Study: Personal Influence, 1945","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0241","justification":"Excellent match. Conducted by Paul F. Lazarsfeld and Elihu Katz in Decatur, Illinois, between June and August 1945, this landmark survey investigates interpersonal influence, opinion leadership, mass media, and social stratification. The study examines how personal relationships and influential individuals shape consumer purchasing decisions, fashion choices, political attitudes, and moviegoing behavior. It includes approximately 800 women aged 16 and older and uses a two-wave panel design to identify changes in opinions and behavior. Respondents identified influential individuals within their social networks, and researchers conducted follow-up interviews with identified opinion leaders to investigate the characteristics and mechanisms of interpersonal influence. Variables address media exposure, social relationships, socioeconomic status, age, family circumstances, and patterns of communication. This is the closest and most comprehensive match to the research requirements. The dataset is archived by GESIS and has DOI 10.4232/1.0241."},{"title":"Erie County Study, 1940 (ICPSR 7204)","url_or_doi":"https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/ICPSR/studies/7204","justification":"Relevant supplementary dataset examining interpersonal influence, social networks, mass media, and political opinion formation during the 1940 presidential election. Conducted in Erie County, Ohio, rather than Illinois, the study investigates how family members, friends, social groups, newspapers, and political communications influence voting intentions and attitudes. Its repeated-interview design allows researchers to examine changes in political preferences and the influence of interpersonal relationships over time. Although it does not cover consumer behavior, fashion, or moviegoing in Decatur, it provides valuable comparative evidence for understanding opinion leadership and the two-step flow of communication during the 1940s."}]}
